# A learned context->answer-profile map does not beat Persona-Vectors' raw prompt projection for trait monitoring, while a direct context->trait predictor beats both (LOW confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v4 -->

## Takeaways

- The learned pre-generation map `h` beat the raw Persona-Vectors monitor by **≥ +0.05** on **0 of 3** traits (evil delta **−0.24 / −0.16**, CIs excluding 0 the WRONG way; sycophancy +0.15 many-shot only; hallucination null) — it FAILED its bar.
- A matched-capacity **direct context->trait predictor dominated the board** — within-condition r **0.91** (sycophancy) and **0.86** (hallucination, system) vs the raw projection's 0.60 / 0.46. The profile-map detour earns nothing when labels exist.
- On held-out behaviors (zero-shot, direct predictor inapplicable), `h` also did NOT beat the raw projection (evil **−0.06** vs 0.17, sycophancy **0.55** vs 0.60, hallucination **0.39** vs 0.46) — the zero-shot value proposition failed too.
- The context DOES linearly reconstruct the answer's mean-activation profile (**R² = 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.86**, above the ~0.10 null; linear beat MLP). A near-perfect reconstruction with a failed trait read means `r_B` lives outside the profile subspace `h` recovers.
- Post-generation mean pooling read the trait better than the prompt (deltas **+0.06 to +0.26**), but this is a near-ceiling reference, not a fair pre-generation monitor.
- **Binding caveat:** the rig-validation gate FAILED — the reproduced raw baseline missed the published table by up to 0.34 (evil system 0.17 vs 0.511), so cross-method comparisons are provisional pending a rig fix.

## Goal

**This experiment in context:** Persona Vectors ([arXiv 2507.21509](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509)) monitors a trait by projecting the last-prompt-token activation onto a persona direction, `⟨c_last, r_B⟩`, and predicting the response's trait score. That read is strong across obviously-different prompts but collapses *within* a condition (their published within-condition r: evil 0.511, sycophancy 0.669, hallucination 0.245 for system-prompt elicitation). This experiment tested two ways to sharpen the within-condition read on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, each against the raw projection AND a matched-capacity direct predictor: (R1) route the projection through a learned, behavior-agnostic map `h: c_x -> v(x)` that predicts the answer's mean-activation profile from the prompt, then read the trait off that prediction; (R2) read the trait off the actual generation's per-token activations (mean/max/top-k/last pooling); (R3) characterize how well the prompt state reconstructs the answer profile at all. It re-extracts the persona directions from scratch per the [persona-vectors recipe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509) rather than reusing any prior in-repo direction.

**Broader narrative:** R1 and R3 are direct instantiations of the project's leakage-theory assumptions — that a pre-fine-tuning context summary predicts the answer-side profile (`v(C) ≈ h(c_C)`) and that each behavior is an approximately linear read-out of that profile (`Expr ≈ r_Bᵀ v(C)`). A learned map that beat the raw projection would be evidence the context state carries recoverable answer-profile content the raw read leaves on the table; a direct predictor that beats the map would localize the map's only value to zero-shot transfer. The result feeds the open question of whether pre-generation representations are a viable monitoring surface for trait/behavior expression at all.

## Methodology

**Design:** No model fine-tuning. Three traits (evil, sycophancy, hallucination) on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16). Persona directions `r_B` re-extracted at all 28 layers. Monitoring evaluated on the Persona-Vectors rig verbatim — two separate elicitation modes evaluated separately: 8 system-prompt conditions and 5 many-shot conditions ({0,5,10,15,20}-shot), 40 eval questions per trait, 10 rollouts per condition-question. The single manipulated variable across the Persona-Vectors / R1 / R2 arms is the **projection input** (raw last-prompt token vs learned-map output vs pooled generation activations); the direction `r_B`, eval rig, judge, model, and layers are held fixed. The learned map `h` and the direct predictor `g` are fit on a disjoint corpus of real user prompts; the exact eval contexts are held out from `h`/`g` training. Read-out layer selected per trait by predictivity over all 28 layers: **evil layer 14, sycophancy layer 26, hallucination layer 17**.

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** The learned map and direct predictor are lightweight regressions over cached activation tensors; their fit constants are in the table below.

| Hyperparameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Model | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16) | plan §10 (repo-standard: #368/#493/#594/#658) |
| `r_B` extraction | 5 pos/neg system-prompt pairs, 20 extraction Qs, 10 rollouts/arm, response-averaged, all 28 layers | persona-vectors-recipe.md / [arXiv 2507.21509](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509) |
| `r_B` judge-filter | keep pos > 50 / neg < 50; REFUSAL / non-numeric / out-of-range DROPPED, never coerced | persona-vectors-recipe.md step 4 |
| Learned map `h` (linear) | ridge, λ by generalized cross-validation, closed-form; input `c_x`, target `v(x)` (mean-response activation) | plan §4.4 (#722 `vectorized_mlp_skill`) |
| Learned map `h` (nonlinear) | MLP, 1 hidden layer × 512 GELU, AdamW lr 1e-3, ≤300 epochs early-stopped, PCA-k multi-output head | plan §4.4 (#722) |
| Direct predictor `g` | matched-capacity ridge AND MLP, `c_x -> trait score`, fit leave-one-context-out on eval contexts | plan §4.4 |
| Read-out | dot `⟨h(c_x), r_B⟩` and cosine `cos(h(c_x), r_B)` (cosine reported, #493) | plan §4.4 |
| Judge | `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, graded 0-100, N=5 draws, temp 1.0, Anthropic Batch API, drop-never-coerce | llm-judging.md rule 1/4/9 |

| Rollout / fit / bootstrap seeds | vLLM/rollout 42, fit 42, bootstrap 0; `max_new_tokens=1024` | plan §10 |
| Bootstrap CI | 95%, resample conditions within-mode, ≥997 valid replicates/cell | plan §6.1 |

**Evaluation:** Primary DV is the trait-expression score — Sonnet graded 0-100, N=5-draw mean, over the model's own 10 on-policy rollouts per condition-question. Primary monitoring metric is within-condition Pearson r (the correlation between a method's monitor score and the judged trait score, computed within each mode's conditions after excluding conditions with trait-score std < 1, averaged within mode), with a 95% bootstrap CI resampling conditions. Secondary detection metrics: AUROC and top-10%-precision per method. R3 map quality: reconstruction R²/cosine of predicted vs true mean-response activation, against a shuffled-context null (20 shuffles). The rig-validation gate requires the reproduced raw-projection within-condition r to land within ±0.10 of the published table; a miss means the extraction/rig diverged and cross-method comparisons are not comparable to the paper.

**Data extraction:** `r_B` directions extracted from on-policy rollouts under 5 contrastive pos/neg system-prompt pairs per trait, judge-filtered (kept pos rollouts: evil 560/1000, sycophancy 242/1000, hallucination 888/1000; the low sycophancy/evil pos-keep reflects the base model rarely expressing the trait even under an eliciting system prompt — a real base-rate signal, drop-never-coerce). The eval pass generated 10 rollouts per condition-question, captured last-prompt and mean-prompt activations at all 28 layers, teacher-forced each rollout to capture the mean-response activation and the mean/max/top-k/last pooled projections onto every-layer `r_B`, and judged each rollout. The `h`/`g` training pass captured `c_x` and `v(x)` at all 28 layers over 5000 real LMSYS prompts.

## Results

### The learned pre-generation map fails to beat the raw projection; the direct predictor beats both (system mode)

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of mean within-condition Pearson r (system-prompt conditions), 95% bootstrap CIs, across six monitors — raw projection, learned map (linear/MLP), direct predictor (linear/MLP), response-mean oracle. n = 8 conditions/trait (fewer survive the std < 1 prune on evil).

![Grouped bars per trait showing the learned map at or below the raw projection while the direct predictor sits far above both](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r1_monitor_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *The learned map does not beat the raw projection; a direct predictor dominates.* Within-condition Pearson r, system-prompt conditions, Qwen-2.5-7B. Learned-map bars (blue) sit at or below the raw projection (orange); the direct predictor (red) reaches 0.91 (sycophancy), 0.86 (hallucination), above the oracle (green). Evil raw 0.17 vs published 0.511.

Interpretation:

- The learned map is negative on evil and at or below the raw read on sycophancy/hallucination — it did not earn its keep.
- The direct predictor dominates: trait predicted directly from `c_x` reaches 0.91 (sycophancy) and 0.86 (hallucination), above the raw projection, the map, and the response-mean oracle.
- So the context carries the trait linearly (the direct probe finds it), but routing through a behavior-agnostic profile reconstruction discards the trait-relevant part.
- The linear-fold nullity check confirms this: the linear map's dot read-out did not match the direct ridge probe (abs difference 0.37-0.67) — a *worse* direction for the trait, not a re-derived better one.

### On held-out behaviors and by success-margin, the map is at or below the raw projection everywhere except one cell

What is plotted (exactly): a forest plot of the success delta (each method's within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection), 95% CIs, for the learned map (linear/MLP) and the response-mean read, in system (blue) and many-shot (red) modes, grouped by trait. Dashed line = parity; dotted line = the +0.05 win threshold.

![Forest plot of method-minus-raw deltas showing learned-map points at or left of zero and post-generation points right of the +0.05 line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r1_success_delta_forest.png)

> **Figure.** *Only post-generation reading clears the +0.05 bar; the learned map falls at or below zero.* Within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection (95% CI); points left of the dashed line are worse than the raw monitor. Learned-map deltas sit at or below zero except sycophancy many-shot; response-mean deltas clear the threshold.

Interpretation:

- The map failed the in-behavior bar (≥ +0.05, CI excluding zero, on ≥2 traits) on 0 of 3 traits. Only positive cell: sycophancy many-shot (+0.15); evil is worse (−0.24 / −0.16); hallucination null.
- Zero-shot held-out-behavior transfer — the map's reason to exist, since the direct predictor is inapplicable there — also failed on every trait (evil −0.06 vs 0.17, sycophancy 0.55 vs 0.60, hallucination 0.39 vs 0.46, system).
- The kernel-ridge rung and a separate labeled in-behavior direct arm were deferred to Stage 2. A kernel map could recover more, but the MLP already underperformed the linear map (next result), arguing against it.

### The prompt state linearly reconstructs the answer's mean-activation profile (R2 = 0.83-0.86)

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of reconstruction R² (predicted vs true mean-response activation) for the linear map (ridge), nonlinear map (MLP), and the shuffled-context null (95th percentile, 20 shuffles). n = held-out contexts.

![Bars showing linear-map R2 0.83-0.86, MLP 0.64-0.71, shuffled null near 0.1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r3_reconstruction_r2.png)

> **Figure.** *The prompt state linearly predicts the answer's mean activation profile.* Reconstruction R² of predicted vs true mean-response activation, held-out contexts. The linear map reaches 0.83-0.86 across traits, beats the nonlinear MLP (0.64-0.71), and both sit far above the shuffled-context null (~0.10-0.15).

Interpretation:

- The characterization half is a clean positive: the context state linearly predicts the answer's mean-activation profile at R² 0.83-0.86, cosine 0.97-0.98, far above the shuffled-context null — direct support for the theory's context->profile-map assumption.
- The linear map beat the nonlinear MLP (0.83 vs 0.68): the map is effectively linear and the MLP underfits; no nonlinear structure to exploit.
- The tension with the monitoring result is informative: `h` reconstructs the profile near-perfectly yet the trait read off it is worse than the raw projection. The trait direction `r_B` lies substantially outside the high-variance profile subspace `h` recovers — reconstructing the dominant directions is not reconstructing the small trait-carrying component. This is the R3(a) slice; per-position decay and set-to-set CKA were deferred to Stage 2.

### Post-generation mean pooling reads the trait better than the prompt projection, as a ceiling reference

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of within-condition Pearson r for five reads — the raw prompt projection and four post-generation poolings (mean, max, top-k, last-response-token) — in system (orange) and many-shot (red) modes, with 95% CIs. n = conditions per mode.

![Grouped bars showing mean pooling above the prompt projection on all traits, last-token unreliable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r2_pooling_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *Post-generation mean pooling reads the trait better than the prompt projection.* Within-condition Pearson r, prompt projection vs generation-pooling reads. Mean pooling clears the prompt projection on all three traits (deltas +0.06 to +0.26); the last-response-token read is unreliable (sycophancy many-shot −0.05).

Interpretation:

- Reading the trait off the generation's per-token activations beats reading the prompt, as expected — the generation nearly contains the answer, so this is a near-ceiling reference, not a fair pre-generation monitor.
- Mean pooling (algebraically the response-mean oracle) beat the raw projection on all three traits (deltas +0.26/+0.19 evil, +0.06/+0.17 sycophancy, +0.15/+0.16 hallucination), clearing +0.10 on evil and hallucination but not sycophancy system.
- Max and top-k did not beat mean, so the max-as-better-detector hypothesis is unsupported at the aggregate level. The last-response-token read is unreliable (sycophancy many-shot −0.05, wide CI) and should not be used.

### The rig-validation gate failed: the reproduced raw-projection baseline diverges from the published table

What is plotted (exactly): a numeric gate, not a figure. Reproduced raw-projection within-condition r vs the published value, per trait-mode; passes only within ±0.10. Missed 4 of 6 (reproduced/published): evil system 0.17/0.511, evil many-shot 0.42/0.735, sycophancy many-shot 0.55/0.813, hallucination system 0.46/0.245 (reversed). Passed: sycophancy system 0.60/0.669, hallucination many-shot 0.30/0.400. `gate1_all_pass = False`.

Interpretation:

## Takeaways

- The learned pre-generation map `h` beat the raw Persona-Vectors monitor by **≥ +0.05** (CI excluding zero) on **2 of 6 in-behavior cells** and **0 of 3 traits** — sycophancy many-shot **+0.15** and hallucination many-shot **+0.12**, both many-shot only; evil is worse (**−0.24 / −0.16**). It FAILED its ≥2-trait bar.
- A matched-capacity **direct context->trait predictor beat every method including the response-mean oracle in all 6 cells** — within-condition r **0.91** (sycophancy) / **0.86** (hallucination, system) vs the raw projection's 0.60 / 0.46 and the oracle's 0.66 / 0.61. On this leave-one-context-out eval scoring, a prompt-only probe out-predicts a read of the actual generation.
- Zero-shot held-out-behavior transfer (`h` applied to an unseen trait, direct predictor inapplicable) failed in system mode on all 3 traits but has ONE many-shot exception: the **linear map reaches 0.70 vs raw 0.55 on sycophancy many-shot**.
- The context DOES linearly reconstruct the answer's mean-activation profile (**R² = 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.86**, far above the ~0.10-0.15 shuffled null; the linear map beat the underfit MLP). The near-perfect reconstruction coexists with a failed trait read — consistent with the trait-relevant directions being poorly recovered by a variance-driven profile fit.
- Post-generation pooling's best operator **flips by trait**: mean pooling wins for sycophancy + hallucination (readily-expressed), but spike reads (last-token / max / top-k) win for evil — the sparse-expression trait — consistent with a spike-detector for sparse behaviors.
- **Binding caveat:** the rig-validation gate FAILED, but the evil miss is dominantly a **layer-selection artifact** — the read-out layer is picked by oracle predictivity, so PV-raw is read off-layer (evil 0.17 at the selected layer vs **0.50** at PV's own best layer, ≈ the published 0.51). Cross-method comparisons stay provisional pending a rig fix.

## Goal

**This experiment in context:** Persona Vectors ([arXiv 2507.21509](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509)) monitors a trait by projecting the last-prompt-token activation onto a persona direction, `⟨c_last, r_B⟩`, and predicting the response's trait score. That read is strong across obviously-different prompts but collapses *within* a condition (their published within-condition r: evil 0.511, sycophancy 0.669, hallucination 0.245 for system-prompt elicitation). This experiment tested two ways to sharpen the within-condition read on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, each against the raw projection AND a matched-capacity direct predictor: (R1) route the projection through a learned, behavior-agnostic map `h: c_x -> v(x)` that predicts the answer's mean-activation profile from the prompt, then read the trait off that prediction; (R2) read the trait off the actual generation's per-token activations (mean/max/top-k/last pooling); (R3) characterize how well the prompt state reconstructs the answer profile at all. It re-extracts the persona directions from scratch per the [persona-vectors recipe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509) rather than reusing any prior in-repo direction. This sits alongside the project's Persona-Vectors replication line ([#778](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/778)); the failed rig-validation gate here (§ below) means it does NOT yet confirm or contradict that replication — the reproduced raw baseline is read at an oracle-selected layer, not PV's own, so absolute anchoring to the paper's table is not yet trustworthy.

**Broader narrative:** R1 and R3 are direct instantiations of the project's leakage-theory assumptions — that a pre-fine-tuning context summary predicts the answer-side profile (`v(C) ≈ h(c_C)`) and that each behavior is an approximately linear read-out of that profile (`Expr ≈ r_Bᵀ v(C)`). A learned map that beat the raw projection would be evidence the context state carries recoverable answer-profile content the raw read leaves on the table; a direct predictor that beats the map would localize the map's only value to zero-shot transfer. The result feeds the open question of whether pre-generation representations are a viable monitoring surface for trait/behavior expression at all.

## Methodology

**Design:** No model fine-tuning. Three traits (evil, sycophancy, hallucination) on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16). Persona directions `r_B` re-extracted at all 28 layers. Monitoring evaluated on the Persona-Vectors rig verbatim — two separate elicitation modes evaluated separately: 8 system-prompt conditions and 5 many-shot conditions ({0,5,10,15,20}-shot), 40 eval questions per trait, 10 rollouts per condition-question. The single manipulated variable across the Persona-Vectors / R1 / R2 arms is the **projection input** (raw last-prompt token vs learned-map output vs pooled generation activations); the direction `r_B`, eval rig, judge, model, and layers are held fixed. The learned map `h` and the direct predictor `g` are fit on a disjoint corpus of real user prompts; the exact eval contexts are held out from `h`/`g` training. Read-out layer selected per trait by **oracle predictivity** over all 28 layers (`issue779_collect.py` selects `argmax_layer oracle_r`): **evil layer 14, sycophancy layer 26, hallucination layer 17**. This oracle-optimal shared layer materially disadvantages the raw prompt projection relative to the generation-based reads — see the rig-gate result below.

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** The learned map and direct predictor are lightweight regressions over cached activation tensors; their fit constants are in the table below.

**Evaluation:** Primary DV is the trait-expression score — Sonnet graded 0-100, N=5-draw mean, over the model's own 10 on-policy rollouts per condition-question. Primary monitoring metric is within-condition Pearson r (the correlation between a method's monitor score and the judged trait score, computed within each mode's conditions after excluding conditions with trait-score std < 1, averaged within mode), with a 95% bootstrap CI resampling conditions. Secondary detection metrics: AUROC and top-10%-precision per method. R3 map quality: reconstruction R²/cosine of predicted vs true mean-response activation, against a shuffled-context null (20 shuffles). The rig-validation gate requires the reproduced raw-projection within-condition r to land within ±0.10 of the published table; a miss means the extraction/rig diverged and cross-method comparisons are not comparable to the paper. **Detection base rates differ sharply and complicate AUROC/top-k reads:** hallucination positives (>50) are 97/160 system and 85/100 many-shot; sycophancy many-shot has only **1/100** positive; evil 29/160 system, 12/100 many-shot. A near-single-positive cell makes top-k precision brittle, so within-condition Pearson r stays the primary metric.

**Data extraction:** `r_B` directions extracted from on-policy rollouts under 5 contrastive pos/neg system-prompt pairs per trait, judge-filtered (kept pos rollouts: evil 560/1000, sycophancy 242/1000, hallucination 888/1000; the low sycophancy/evil pos-keep reflects the base model rarely expressing the trait even under an eliciting system prompt — a real base-rate signal, drop-never-coerce). The eval pass generated 10 rollouts per condition-question, captured last-prompt and mean-prompt activations at all 28 layers, teacher-forced each rollout to capture the mean-response activation and the mean/max/top-k/last pooled projections onto every-layer `r_B`, and judged each rollout (46 judge returns dropped, never coerced). The `h`/`g` training pass captured `c_x` and `v(x)` at all 28 layers over 5000 real LMSYS prompts.

## Results

### The learned pre-generation map fails to beat the raw projection; the direct predictor beats every method including the oracle (system mode)

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of within-condition Pearson r (system, 95% CIs) across six monitors — raw projection, learned map (linear/MLP), direct predictor (linear/MLP), oracle. n = 8 conditions/trait (evil keeps 4 after the std < 1 prune).

![Per-trait monitor comparison bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r1_monitor_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *The learned map does not beat the raw projection; a direct predictor dominates.* Within-condition Pearson r, system-prompt conditions, Qwen-2.5-7B. Learned-map bars (blue) sit at or below the raw projection (orange); the direct predictor (red) reaches 0.91 (sycophancy), 0.86 (hallucination), above the oracle (green). Evil raw 0.17 at the oracle-selected layer.

Interpretation:

- The learned map is negative on evil and at or below the raw read on sycophancy/hallucination (system) — it did not earn its keep.
- The direct predictor beats every method including the oracle in all 6 cells (sycophancy **0.91** vs oracle 0.66; hallucination **0.86** vs 0.61). A prompt-only probe out-predicting a read of the actual generation is the strongest positive — the prompt fixes the trait more sharply than the generation.
- The context carries the trait linearly, yet routing through the profile reconstruction discards the trait-relevant part: the map's dot read-out did not match the direct probe (abs difference **0.20-0.67** across cells).
- Scope caveat: the direct predictor is scored leave-one-context-out (the labeled in-behavior arm is deferred to Stage 2), so this dominance is a LOCO-eval claim, not a general one.

### On held-out behaviors and by success-margin, the map beats the raw projection in two many-shot cells only

What is plotted (exactly): a forest plot of the success delta (each method's within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection, 95% CIs) for the learned map (linear/MLP) and the response-mean read, in system and many-shot modes, grouped by trait. Dashed line = parity; dotted line = the +0.05 win threshold.

![Success-delta forest plot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r1_success_delta_forest.png)

> **Figure.** *The learned map clears the +0.05 bar in two many-shot cells only; post-generation reading clears it broadly.* Within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection (95% CI); points left of the dashed line are worse than the raw monitor. Learned-map deltas sit at or below zero except sycophancy many-shot (+0.15) and hallucination many-shot (+0.12); response-mean deltas clear the threshold.

Interpretation:

- The map failed the in-behavior bar (≥ +0.05, CI excluding zero, ≥2 traits): it clears **2 of 6 cells**, both many-shot — sycophancy (**+0.15**) and hallucination (**+0.12**). Evil is worse in both modes (−0.24 / −0.16); every system-mode learned-map cell is at or below zero.
- Zero-shot held-out-behavior transfer (the map's reason to exist) failed in system mode on all 3 traits, but has ONE many-shot exception: **sycophancy many-shot = 0.70 vs raw 0.55**. Evil and hallucination many-shot still fail.
- Kernel-ridge and a labeled in-behavior direct arm are deferred to Stage 2; a kernel map could recover more, but the MLP already underperformed the linear map (next result), arguing against it.

### The prompt state linearly reconstructs the answer's mean-activation profile (R2 = 0.83-0.86)

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of reconstruction R² (predicted vs true mean-response activation) for the linear map (ridge), the MLP, and the shuffled-context null (95th pct, 20 shuffles). n = held-out contexts.

![Reconstruction R2 bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r3_reconstruction_r2.png)

> **Figure.** *The prompt state linearly predicts the answer's mean activation profile.* Reconstruction R² of predicted vs true mean-response activation, held-out contexts. The linear map reaches 0.83-0.86 across traits, beats the nonlinear MLP (0.64-0.71), and both sit far above the shuffled-context null (~0.10-0.15).

Interpretation:

- A clean positive: the context state linearly predicts the answer's mean-activation profile at R² 0.83-0.86, cosine 0.97-0.98, far above the shuffled null (p95 0.10-0.15) — direct support for the context->profile-map assumption.
- The linear map beat the MLP (0.83 vs 0.68): the linear fit dominates and the MLP underfits. This MLP was not extensively tuned and kernel-ridge is deferred, so the read is "linear suffices", not "no nonlinear structure exists".
- The tension with the monitoring result is informative: `h` reconstructs the profile near-perfectly yet the trait read off it is worse than the raw projection — consistent with `r_B` being poorly recovered by the variance-driven fit (a high global R² can miss the low-variance trait component). Whether `r_B` lies outside the recovered subspace is a hypothesis this metric does not establish; the subspace-overlap read is deferred to Stage 2.

### Post-generation pooling reads the trait better than the prompt, and its best operator flips by trait

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of within-condition Pearson r for five reads — raw prompt projection and four post-generation poolings (mean, max, top-k, last-token) — in system and many-shot modes, 95% CIs. n = conditions per mode.

![Pooling-operator comparison bars per trait](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/3b1e7907e59c93a3b52a45c5c7cfd07cb97ab04e/figures/issue_779/r2_pooling_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *The best pooling operator flips by trait.* Within-condition Pearson r, prompt projection vs generation-pooling reads. Mean pooling wins for sycophancy + hallucination; for evil the spike reads (last-token 0.61/0.76, max/top-k ~0.53) beat mean (0.43), and sycophancy last-token collapses (many-shot −0.05).

Interpretation:

- Reading the trait off the generation's per-token activations beats the prompt — the generation nearly contains the answer, so this is a near-ceiling reference, not a fair pre-generation monitor.
- **The best pooling operator flips by trait.** For sycophancy + hallucination (readily-expressed) mean pooling (algebraically the oracle) wins. For **evil** (sparse expression) the spike reads win: last-token **0.61/0.76** is the single best evil read, max/top-k (~0.53) also beat mean (0.43) — consistent with the plan's spike-detector hypothesis for sparse behaviors.
- Conversely, last-token is the WORST read for the readily-expressed traits (sycophancy 0.23 system, **−0.05** many-shot): the choice tracks base-expression sparsity.
- Alternative not ruled out: these reads could partly reflect nuisance structure (length, refusal style, condition identity) rather than trait content; a length/condition-control follow-up is deferred to Stage 2.

### The rig-validation gate failed: the raw baseline is read at the oracle-selected layer, not its own best layer

What is plotted (exactly): a numeric gate. Reproduced raw-projection within-condition r vs published, per trait-mode (±0.10 band). Missed 4 of 6 trait-modes (only sycophancy system, hallucination many-shot passed). `gate1_all_pass = False`. Table: raw at the oracle-selected layer vs its own best layer.

| Trait-mode | selected layer | raw @ selected | raw @ own best | published |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| evil system | L14 | 0.17 | **0.50** (L20) | 0.511 |
| evil many-shot | L14 | 0.42 | 0.62 (L19) | 0.735 |
| hallucination system | L17 | 0.46 | **0.56** (L24) | 0.245 |
| hallucination many-shot | L17 | 0.30 | 0.53 (L27) | 0.400 |

Interpretation:

- The binding constraint: a > 0.10 miss means absolute anchoring to Persona-Vectors' numbers is not yet trustworthy, holding the LOW tag.
- **The dominant cause is layer selection, not base-rate collapse.** The read-out layer is picked by oracle predictivity, but the raw projection's own best layer is elsewhere (table): evil recovers to 0.50 at its own layer 20. Evil's miss is almost entirely a layer-selection artifact, and it weakens the "no method gap is manufactured" defense — the shared oracle-optimal layer favors the mean/oracle reads while the raw projection is read off-layer.
- Base-rate collapse is a secondary evil factor (4 of 8 conditions prune below std 1); hallucination above published at its best layer suggests a rig difference too. Reading each method at its own optimal layer is the prerequisite for a MODERATE read.

# A learned context->answer-profile map does not beat Persona-Vectors' raw prompt projection for trait monitoring, while a direct context->trait predictor beats both (LOW confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v4 -->

## Takeaways

- The learned pre-generation map `h` beat the raw Persona-Vectors monitor by **≥ +0.05** (CI excluding zero) on **2 of 6 in-behavior cells** and **0 of 3 traits** — sycophancy many-shot **+0.15** (the linear map) and hallucination many-shot **+0.12** (the underfit MLP variant), both many-shot only; evil is worse (**−0.24 / −0.16**). It FAILED its ≥2-trait bar.
- A matched-capacity **direct context->trait predictor beat every method at point estimate in all 6 cells, and beat the oracle CI-separated in 4 of 6** (sycophancy + hallucination, both modes; the 2 evil cells are within CI noise) — within-condition r **0.91** (sycophancy) / **0.86** (hallucination, system) vs the raw projection's 0.60 / 0.46 and the oracle's 0.66 / 0.61. On this leave-one-context-out eval scoring, a prompt-only probe out-predicts a read of the actual generation.
- Zero-shot held-out-behavior transfer (`h` applied to an unseen trait, direct predictor inapplicable) failed in system mode on all 3 traits but has ONE many-shot exception: the **linear map reaches 0.70 vs raw 0.55 on sycophancy many-shot**.
- The context linearly reconstructs the **TRAINING** answer profile in-sample (**R² = 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.86**, an in-sample diagnostic, well above the ~0.10-0.15 shuffled-pairing null — so the ridge uses context-specific information, not the marginal answer profile; the linear map beat the underfit MLP). This is NOT held-out generalization, and it coexists with a failed trait read — consistent with a variance-driven profile fit that recovers the profile's bulk while missing the low-variance trait direction.
- Post-generation pooling's best operator **flips by trait**: mean pooling wins for sycophancy + hallucination (readily-expressed), but spike reads (last-token / max / top-k) win for evil — the sparse-expression trait — consistent with a spike-detector for sparse behaviors.
- **Binding caveat:** the rig-validation gate FAILED, with **multiple causes**. Layer selection explains the evil case (PV-raw is read off-layer at the oracle-selected layer: evil system 0.17 vs **0.50** at PV's own best layer, ≈ the published 0.51). But it does NOT fully explain the rest: sycophancy many-shot stays **0.21 below** the paper even at PV's own best layer, and hallucination system is **above** the paper at its own best layer — so rig differences beyond layer choice also contribute. Cross-method comparisons stay provisional pending a rig fix.

## Goal

**This experiment in context:** Persona Vectors ([arXiv 2507.21509](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509)) monitors a trait by projecting the last-prompt-token activation onto a persona direction, `⟨c_last, r_B⟩`, and predicting the response's trait score. That read is strong across obviously-different prompts but collapses *within* a condition (their published within-condition r: evil 0.511, sycophancy 0.669, hallucination 0.245 for system-prompt elicitation). This experiment tested two ways to sharpen the within-condition read on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, each against the raw projection AND a matched-capacity direct predictor: (R1) route the projection through a learned, behavior-agnostic map `h: c_x -> v(x)` that predicts the answer's mean-activation profile from the prompt, then read the trait off that prediction; (R2) read the trait off the actual generation's per-token activations (mean/max/top-k/last pooling); (R3) characterize how well the prompt state reconstructs the answer profile at all. It re-extracts the persona directions from scratch per the [persona-vectors recipe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509) rather than reusing any prior in-repo direction. This sits alongside the project's Persona-Vectors replication line ([#778](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/778)); the failed rig-validation gate here (§ below) means it does NOT yet confirm or contradict that replication — the reproduced raw baseline is read at an oracle-selected layer, not PV's own, so absolute anchoring to the paper's table is not yet trustworthy.

**Broader narrative:** R1 and R3 are direct instantiations of the project's leakage-theory assumptions — that a pre-fine-tuning context summary predicts the answer-side profile (`v(C) ≈ h(c_C)`) and that each behavior is an approximately linear read-out of that profile (`Expr ≈ r_Bᵀ v(C)`). A learned map that beat the raw projection would be evidence the context state carries recoverable answer-profile content the raw read leaves on the table; a direct predictor that beats the map would localize the map's only value to zero-shot transfer. The result feeds the open question of whether pre-generation representations are a viable monitoring surface for trait/behavior expression at all.

## Methodology

**Design:** No model fine-tuning. Three traits (evil, sycophancy, hallucination) on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16). Persona directions `r_B` re-extracted at all 28 layers. Monitoring evaluated on the Persona-Vectors rig verbatim — two separate elicitation modes evaluated separately: 8 system-prompt conditions and 5 many-shot conditions ({0,5,10,15,20}-shot), 40 eval questions per trait, 10 rollouts per condition-question. The single manipulated variable across the Persona-Vectors / R1 / R2 arms is the **projection input** (raw last-prompt token vs learned-map output vs pooled generation activations); the direction `r_B`, eval rig, judge, model, and layers are held fixed. The learned map `h` and the direct predictor `g` are fit on a disjoint corpus of real user prompts; the exact eval contexts are held out from `h`/`g` training. Read-out layer selected per trait by **oracle predictivity** over all 28 layers (`issue779_collect.py` selects `argmax_layer oracle_r`): **evil layer 14, sycophancy layer 26, hallucination layer 17**. This oracle-optimal shared layer materially disadvantages the raw prompt projection relative to the generation-based reads — see the rig-gate result below.

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** The learned map and direct predictor are lightweight regressions over cached activation tensors; their fit constants are in the table below.

**Evaluation:** Primary DV is the trait-expression score — Sonnet graded 0-100, N=5-draw mean, over the model's own 10 on-policy rollouts per condition-question. Primary monitoring metric is within-condition Pearson r (the correlation between a method's monitor score and the judged trait score, computed within each mode's conditions after excluding conditions with trait-score std < 1, averaged within mode), with a 95% bootstrap CI resampling conditions. Secondary detection metrics: AUROC and top-10%-precision per method. R3 map quality: **in-sample** reconstruction R²/cosine of predicted vs true mean-response activation (the ridge/MLP is fit and read on the same training contexts — the eval side has no true `v(x)` at `c_last`, a `stage1.py:253-256` constraint, so held-out reconstruction is not reported), against a shuffled-pairing null (20 row-permuted context->answer pairings). The rig-validation gate requires the reproduced raw-projection within-condition r to land within ±0.10 of the published table; a miss means the extraction/rig diverged and cross-method comparisons are not comparable to the paper. **Detection base rates differ sharply and complicate AUROC/top-k reads:** hallucination positives (>50) are 97/160 system and 85/100 many-shot; sycophancy many-shot has only **1/100** positive; evil 29/160 system, 12/100 many-shot. A near-single-positive cell makes top-k precision brittle, so within-condition Pearson r stays the primary metric.

**Data extraction:** `r_B` directions extracted from on-policy rollouts under 5 contrastive pos/neg system-prompt pairs per trait, judge-filtered (kept pos rollouts: evil 560/1000, sycophancy 242/1000, hallucination 888/1000; the low sycophancy/evil pos-keep reflects the base model rarely expressing the trait even under an eliciting system prompt — a real base-rate signal, drop-never-coerce). The eval pass generated 10 rollouts per condition-question, captured last-prompt and mean-prompt activations at all 28 layers, teacher-forced each rollout to capture the mean-response activation and the mean/max/top-k/last pooled projections onto every-layer `r_B`, and judged each rollout (46 judge returns dropped, never coerced). The `h`/`g` training pass captured `c_x` and `v(x)` at all 28 layers over 5000 real LMSYS prompts.

## Results

### The learned map fails to beat the raw projection; the direct predictor tops every method (system mode; CI-separated from the oracle for sycophancy + hallucination)

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of within-condition Pearson r (system, 95% CIs) across six monitors — raw projection, learned map (linear/MLP), direct predictor (linear/MLP), oracle. n = 8 conditions/trait (evil keeps 4 after the std < 1 prune).

![Per-trait monitor comparison bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r1_monitor_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *The learned map does not beat the raw projection; a direct predictor dominates.* Within-condition Pearson r, system-prompt conditions, Qwen-2.5-7B. Learned-map bars (blue) sit at or below the raw projection (orange); the direct predictor (red) reaches 0.91 (sycophancy), 0.86 (hallucination), above the oracle (green). Evil raw 0.17 at the oracle-selected layer.

Interpretation:

- The learned map is negative on evil and at or below the raw read on sycophancy/hallucination (system).
- The direct predictor beats every method at point estimate in all 6 cells (sycophancy **0.91** vs oracle 0.66; hallucination **0.86** vs 0.61), and beats the oracle CI-separated in 4 of 6 (sycophancy + hallucination, both modes); the 2 evil cells are within CI noise (the wide evil many-shot oracle CI, 0.26 to 0.87, contains the direct point). A prompt-only probe out-predicting a generation read is the strongest positive.
- Routing through profile reconstruction discards the trait-relevant part: the map's dot read-out did not match the direct probe (abs diff **0.20-0.67**).
- Scope caveat: the direct predictor is scored leave-one-context-out (labeled in-behavior arm deferred), so this dominance is a LOCO-eval claim, not general.

### On held-out behaviors and by success-margin, the map beats the raw projection in two many-shot cells only

What is plotted (exactly): a forest plot of the success delta (each method's within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection, 95% CIs) for the learned map (linear/MLP) and the response-mean read, both modes, grouped by trait. Dashed = parity; dotted = the +0.05 win threshold.

![Success-delta forest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/37e1a1cace7e54ab5aaf3233497b49a25ed4cf34/figures/issue_779/r1_success_delta_forest.png)

> **Figure.** *The learned map clears the +0.05 bar in 2 of 6 cells (sycophancy many-shot, hallucination many-shot); post-generation reading clears it broadly.* Within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection (95% CI); points left of the dashed line are worse than the raw monitor. Learned-map deltas are at or below zero in the 4 remaining cells; the 2 positive cells are sycophancy many-shot (+0.15, linear map) and hallucination many-shot (+0.12, MLP variant); response-mean deltas clear the threshold.

Interpretation:

- The map failed the in-behavior bar (≥ +0.05, CI excluding zero, ≥2 traits): it clears **2 of 6 cells**, both many-shot — sycophancy **+0.15** (the LINEAR map) and hallucination **+0.12** (the MLP variant; the linear map fails on hallucination). No single map variant clears the bar on ≥2 traits. Evil is worse in both modes (−0.24 / −0.16); every system-mode cell is at or below zero.
- Zero-shot held-out-behavior transfer (the map's reason to exist) failed in system mode on all 3 traits, with ONE many-shot exception: **sycophancy many-shot = 0.70 vs raw 0.55**. Evil and hallucination many-shot still fail.
- Kernel-ridge and a labeled in-behavior direct arm are deferred to Stage 2; the MLP already underperformed the linear map (next result), arguing against a kernel map recovering much more.

### The prompt state linearly reconstructs the TRAINING answer profile in-sample (R2 = 0.83-0.86), above a shuffled-pairing null

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of in-sample reconstruction R² for the linear map (ridge), the MLP, and a shuffled-pairing null (p95, 20 row-permuted pairings). The map is fit and read on the SAME training contexts. n = training contexts.

![Reconstruction R2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/37e1a1cace7e54ab5aaf3233497b49a25ed4cf34/figures/issue_779/r3_reconstruction_r2.png)

> **Figure.** *In-sample, the prompt state linearly predicts the training answer's mean activation profile.* In-sample reconstruction R² of predicted vs true mean-response activation, fit and read on the same training contexts. The linear map reaches 0.83-0.86 across traits, beats the nonlinear MLP (0.64-0.71), and both sit far above the shuffled-pairing null (~0.10-0.15) — so the fit uses context-specific information, not the marginal answer profile.

Interpretation:

- Narrow claim: in-sample, the context state linearly predicts the training answer's mean-activation profile (R² 0.83-0.86, cosine 0.97-0.98). This is a train-fit diagnostic, NOT held-out generalization — the eval side has no true `v(x)` at `c_last` (`stage1.py:253-256`).
- Beating the shuffled-pairing null (p95 0.10-0.15) is a real but weaker positive: the ridge uses context-SPECIFIC information, not the marginal profile — but does not show the fit generalizes. Read 0.83-0.86 as an in-sample upper bound.
- The linear map beat the MLP (0.83 vs 0.68) in-sample; the MLP underfits, so "linear suffices in-sample".
- The tension with monitoring stands even in-sample: `h` reconstructs the profile near-perfectly yet the trait read off it trails the raw projection — consistent with `r_B` poorly recovered by a variance-driven fit. A held-out arm is deferred to Stage 2.

### Post-generation pooling reads the trait better than the prompt, and its best operator flips by trait

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of within-condition Pearson r for five reads — raw prompt projection and four post-generation poolings (mean, max, top-k, last-token) — in system and many-shot modes, 95% CIs. n = conditions per mode.

![Pooling-operator comparison bars per trait](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/3b1e7907e59c93a3b52a45c5c7cfd07cb97ab04e/figures/issue_779/r2_pooling_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *The best pooling operator flips by trait.* Within-condition Pearson r, prompt projection vs generation-pooling reads. Mean pooling wins for sycophancy + hallucination; for evil the spike reads (last-token 0.61/0.76, max/top-k ~0.53) beat mean (0.43), and sycophancy last-token collapses (many-shot −0.05).

Interpretation:

- Reading the trait off the generation's per-token activations beats the prompt — the generation nearly contains the answer, so this is a near-ceiling reference, not a fair pre-generation monitor.
- **The best pooling operator flips by trait.** For sycophancy + hallucination (readily-expressed) mean pooling (algebraically the oracle) wins. For **evil** (sparse expression) the spike reads win: last-token **0.61/0.76** is the single best evil read, max/top-k (~0.53) also beat mean (0.43) — consistent with the plan's spike-detector hypothesis for sparse behaviors.
- Conversely, last-token is the WORST read for the readily-expressed traits (sycophancy 0.23 system, **−0.05** many-shot): the choice tracks base-expression sparsity.
- Alternative not ruled out: these reads could partly reflect nuisance structure (length, refusal style, condition identity) rather than trait content; a length/condition-control follow-up is deferred to Stage 2.

### The rig-validation gate failed, with multiple causes beyond layer selection

What is plotted (exactly): a numeric gate. Reproduced raw-projection within-condition r vs published, per trait-mode (±0.10 band); missed 4 of 6 (`gate1_all_pass = False`). The table adds raw at the oracle-selected layer vs its own best layer.

| evil many-shot | L14 | 0.42 | 0.62 (L19) | 0.735 |

Interpretation:

- Binding constraint: a > 0.10 miss means anchoring to Persona-Vectors' numbers is not yet trustworthy, holding the LOW tag.
- **The rig-gate failure has multiple causes.** Layer selection explains EVIL: the oracle-picked layer reads the raw projection off-layer, and evil recovers 0.17 → 0.50 at its own best layer 20 (≈ the published 0.51).
- But layer selection does NOT close the gap elsewhere. Even at PV's OWN best layer (table), sycophancy many-shot reaches only 0.60 vs the published 0.813 (0.21 short) and hallucination system 0.56, ABOVE the published 0.245 — so rig differences beyond layer choice contribute in both directions.
- Base-rate collapse is a further evil-specific factor (4 of 8 conditions prune below std 1). Reading each method at its own optimal layer AND resolving the residual rig differences are prerequisites for a MODERATE read.

# A learned context->answer-profile map does not beat Persona-Vectors' raw prompt projection for trait monitoring, while a direct context->trait predictor beats both (LOW confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v4 -->

## Takeaways

- The learned pre-generation map `h` beat the raw Persona-Vectors monitor by **≥ +0.05** (CI excluding zero) on **2 of 6 in-behavior cells** and **0 of 3 traits** — sycophancy many-shot **+0.15** (the linear map) and hallucination many-shot **+0.12** (the underfit MLP variant), both many-shot only; evil is worse (**−0.24 / −0.16**). It FAILED its ≥2-trait bar.
- A matched-capacity **direct context->trait predictor beat every pre-generation method at point estimate in all 6 cells, and beat the oracle CI-separated in 4 of 6** (sycophancy + hallucination, both modes; the 2 evil cells are within CI noise; post-generation r2_last actually leads direct on evil at point estimate — 0.61 sys / 0.76 many-shot vs direct 0.54 / 0.71, per Result 4) — within-condition r **0.91** (sycophancy) / **0.86** (hallucination, system) vs the raw projection's 0.60 / 0.46 and the oracle's 0.66 / 0.61. On this leave-one-context-out eval scoring, a prompt-only probe out-predicts every read of the actual generation on non-evil traits; only post-generation r2_last on evil beats it.
- Zero-shot held-out-behavior transfer (`h` applied to an unseen trait, direct predictor inapplicable) failed in system mode on all 3 traits but has ONE many-shot exception: the **linear map reaches 0.70 vs raw 0.55 on sycophancy many-shot**.
- The context linearly reconstructs the **TRAINING** answer profile in-sample (**R² = 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.86**, an in-sample diagnostic, well above the ~0.10-0.15 shuffled-pairing null — so the ridge uses context-specific information, not the marginal answer profile; the linear map beat the underfit MLP). This is NOT held-out generalization, and it coexists with a failed trait read — consistent with a variance-driven profile fit that recovers the profile's bulk while missing the low-variance trait direction.
- Post-generation pooling's best operator **flips by trait**: mean pooling wins for sycophancy + hallucination (readily-expressed), but spike reads (last-token / max / top-k) win for evil — the sparse-expression trait — consistent with a spike-detector for sparse behaviors.
- **Binding caveat:** the rig-validation gate FAILED, with **multiple causes**. Layer selection explains the evil case (PV-raw is read off-layer at the oracle-selected layer: evil system 0.17 vs **0.50** at PV's own best layer, ≈ the published 0.51). But it does NOT fully explain the rest: sycophancy many-shot stays **0.21 below** the paper even at PV's own best layer, and hallucination system is **above** the paper at its own best layer — so rig differences beyond layer choice also contribute. Cross-method comparisons stay provisional pending a rig fix.

## Goal

**This experiment in context:** Persona Vectors ([arXiv 2507.21509](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509)) monitors a trait by projecting the last-prompt-token activation onto a persona direction, `⟨c_last, r_B⟩`, and predicting the response's trait score. That read is strong across obviously-different prompts but collapses *within* a condition (their published within-condition r: evil 0.511, sycophancy 0.669, hallucination 0.245 for system-prompt elicitation). This experiment tested two ways to sharpen the within-condition read on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, each against the raw projection AND a matched-capacity direct predictor: (R1) route the projection through a learned, behavior-agnostic map `h: c_x -> v(x)` that predicts the answer's mean-activation profile from the prompt, then read the trait off that prediction; (R2) read the trait off the actual generation's per-token activations (mean/max/top-k/last pooling); (R3) characterize how well the prompt state reconstructs the answer profile at all. It re-extracts the persona directions from scratch per the [persona-vectors recipe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21509) rather than reusing any prior in-repo direction. This sits alongside the project's Persona-Vectors replication line ([#778](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/778)); the failed rig-validation gate here (§ below) means it does NOT yet confirm or contradict that replication — the reproduced raw baseline is read at an oracle-selected layer, not PV's own, so absolute anchoring to the paper's table is not yet trustworthy.

**Broader narrative:** R1 and R3 are direct instantiations of the project's leakage-theory assumptions — that a pre-fine-tuning context summary predicts the answer-side profile (`v(C) ≈ h(c_C)`) and that each behavior is an approximately linear read-out of that profile (`Expr ≈ r_Bᵀ v(C)`). A learned map that beat the raw projection would be evidence the context state carries recoverable answer-profile content the raw read leaves on the table; a direct predictor that beats the map would localize the map's only value to zero-shot transfer. The result feeds the open question of whether pre-generation representations are a viable monitoring surface for trait/behavior expression at all.

## Methodology

**Design:** No model fine-tuning. Three traits (evil, sycophancy, hallucination) on `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16). Persona directions `r_B` re-extracted at all 28 layers. Monitoring evaluated on the Persona-Vectors rig verbatim — two separate elicitation modes evaluated separately: 8 system-prompt conditions and 5 many-shot conditions ({0,5,10,15,20}-shot), 40 eval questions per trait, 10 rollouts per condition-question. The single manipulated variable across the Persona-Vectors / R1 / R2 arms is the **projection input** (raw last-prompt token vs learned-map output vs pooled generation activations); the direction `r_B`, eval rig, judge, model, and layers are held fixed. The learned map `h` and the direct predictor `g` are fit on a disjoint corpus of real user prompts; the exact eval contexts are held out from `h`/`g` training. Read-out layer selected per trait by **oracle predictivity** over all 28 layers (`issue779_collect.py` selects `argmax_layer oracle_r`): **evil layer 14, sycophancy layer 26, hallucination layer 17**. This oracle-optimal shared layer materially disadvantages the raw prompt projection relative to the generation-based reads — see the rig-gate result below.

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** The learned map and direct predictor are lightweight regressions over cached activation tensors; their fit constants are in the table below.

**Evaluation:** Primary DV is the trait-expression score — Sonnet graded 0-100, N=5-draw mean, over the model's own 10 on-policy rollouts per condition-question. Primary monitoring metric is within-condition Pearson r (the correlation between a method's monitor score and the judged trait score, computed within each mode's conditions after excluding conditions with trait-score std < 1, averaged within mode), with a 95% bootstrap CI resampling conditions. Secondary detection metrics: AUROC and top-10%-precision per method. R3 map quality: **in-sample** reconstruction R²/cosine of predicted vs true mean-response activation (the ridge/MLP is fit and read on the same training contexts — the eval side has no true `v(x)` at `c_last`, a `stage1.py:253-256` constraint, so held-out reconstruction is not reported), against a shuffled-pairing null (20 row-permuted context->answer pairings). The rig-validation gate requires the reproduced raw-projection within-condition r to land within ±0.10 of the published table; a miss means the extraction/rig diverged and cross-method comparisons are not comparable to the paper. **Detection base rates differ sharply and complicate AUROC/top-k reads:** hallucination positives (>50) are 97/160 system and 85/100 many-shot; sycophancy many-shot has only **1/100** positive; evil 29/160 system, 12/100 many-shot. A near-single-positive cell makes top-k precision brittle, so within-condition Pearson r stays the primary metric.

**Data extraction:** `r_B` directions extracted from on-policy rollouts under 5 contrastive pos/neg system-prompt pairs per trait, judge-filtered (kept pos rollouts: evil 560/1000, sycophancy 242/1000, hallucination 888/1000; the low sycophancy/evil pos-keep reflects the base model rarely expressing the trait even under an eliciting system prompt — a real base-rate signal, drop-never-coerce). The eval pass generated 10 rollouts per condition-question, captured last-prompt and mean-prompt activations at all 28 layers, teacher-forced each rollout to capture the mean-response activation and the mean/max/top-k/last pooled projections onto every-layer `r_B`, and judged each rollout (46 judge returns dropped, never coerced). The `h`/`g` training pass captured `c_x` and `v(x)` at all 28 layers over 5000 real LMSYS prompts.

## Results

### The learned map fails to beat the raw projection; the direct predictor tops every method (system mode; CI-separated from the oracle for sycophancy + hallucination)

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of within-condition Pearson r (system, 95% CIs) across six monitors — raw projection, learned map (linear/MLP), direct predictor (linear/MLP), oracle. n = 8 conditions/trait (evil keeps 4 after the std < 1 prune).

![Per-trait monitor comparison bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/39baa0ce98c22b5d7c8be4ac05710db1b8940f23/figures/issue_779/r1_monitor_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *The learned map does not beat the raw projection; a direct predictor dominates.* Within-condition Pearson r, system-prompt conditions, Qwen-2.5-7B. Learned-map bars (blue) sit at or below the raw projection (orange); the direct predictor (red) reaches 0.91 (sycophancy), 0.86 (hallucination), above the oracle (green). Evil raw 0.17 at the oracle-selected layer.

Interpretation:

- The learned map is negative on evil and at or below the raw read on sycophancy/hallucination (system).
- The direct predictor beats every method at point estimate in all 6 cells (sycophancy **0.91** vs oracle 0.66; hallucination **0.86** vs 0.61), and beats the oracle CI-separated in 4 of 6 (sycophancy + hallucination, both modes); the 2 evil cells are within CI noise (the wide evil many-shot oracle CI, 0.26 to 0.87, contains the direct point). A prompt-only probe out-predicting a generation read is the strongest positive.
- Routing through profile reconstruction discards the trait-relevant part: the map's dot read-out did not match the direct probe (abs diff **0.20-0.67**).
- Scope caveat: the direct predictor is scored leave-one-context-out (labeled in-behavior arm deferred), so this dominance is a LOCO-eval claim, not general.

### On held-out behaviors and by success-margin, the map beats the raw projection in two many-shot cells only

What is plotted (exactly): a forest plot of the success delta (each method's within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection, 95% CIs) for the learned map (linear/MLP) and the response-mean read, both modes, grouped by trait. Dashed = parity; dotted = the +0.05 win threshold.

![Success-delta forest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/37e1a1cace7e54ab5aaf3233497b49a25ed4cf34/figures/issue_779/r1_success_delta_forest.png)

> **Figure.** *The learned map clears the +0.05 bar in 2 of 6 cells (sycophancy many-shot, hallucination many-shot); post-generation reading clears it broadly.* Within-condition Pearson r minus the raw projection (95% CI); points left of the dashed line are worse than the raw monitor. Learned-map deltas are at or below zero in the 4 remaining cells; the 2 positive cells are sycophancy many-shot (+0.15, linear map) and hallucination many-shot (+0.12, MLP variant); response-mean deltas clear the threshold.

Interpretation:

- The map failed the in-behavior bar (≥ +0.05, CI excluding zero, ≥2 traits): it clears **2 of 6 cells**, both many-shot — sycophancy **+0.15** (the LINEAR map) and hallucination **+0.12** (the MLP variant; the linear map fails on hallucination). No single map variant clears the bar on ≥2 traits. Evil is worse in both modes (−0.24 / −0.16); every system-mode cell is at or below zero.
- Zero-shot held-out-behavior transfer (the map's reason to exist) failed in system mode on all 3 traits, with ONE many-shot exception: **sycophancy many-shot = 0.70 vs raw 0.55**. Evil and hallucination many-shot still fail.
- Kernel-ridge and a labeled in-behavior direct arm are deferred to Stage 2; the MLP already underperformed the linear map (next result), arguing against a kernel map recovering much more.

### The prompt state linearly reconstructs the TRAINING answer profile in-sample (R2 = 0.83-0.86), above a shuffled-pairing null

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of in-sample reconstruction R² for the linear map (ridge), the MLP, and a shuffled-pairing null (p95, 20 row-permuted pairings). The map is fit and read on the SAME training contexts. n = training contexts.

![Reconstruction R2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/37e1a1cace7e54ab5aaf3233497b49a25ed4cf34/figures/issue_779/r3_reconstruction_r2.png)

> **Figure.** *In-sample, the prompt state linearly predicts the training answer's mean activation profile.* In-sample reconstruction R² of predicted vs true mean-response activation, fit and read on the same training contexts. The linear map reaches 0.83-0.86 across traits, beats the nonlinear MLP (0.64-0.71), and both sit far above the shuffled-pairing null (~0.10-0.15) — so the fit uses context-specific information, not the marginal answer profile.

Interpretation:

- Narrow claim: in-sample, the context state linearly predicts the training answer's mean-activation profile (R² 0.83-0.86, cosine 0.97-0.98). This is a train-fit diagnostic, NOT held-out generalization — the eval side has no true `v(x)` at `c_last` (`stage1.py:253-256`).
- Beating the shuffled-pairing null (p95 0.10-0.15) is a real but weaker positive: the ridge uses context-SPECIFIC information, not the marginal profile — but does not show the fit generalizes. Read 0.83-0.86 as an in-sample upper bound.
- The linear map beat the MLP (0.83 vs 0.68) in-sample; the MLP underfits, so "linear suffices in-sample".
- The tension with monitoring stands even in-sample: `h` reconstructs the profile near-perfectly yet the trait read off it trails the raw projection — consistent with `r_B` poorly recovered by a variance-driven fit. A held-out arm is deferred to Stage 2.

### Post-generation pooling reads the trait better than the prompt, and its best operator flips by trait

What is plotted (exactly): per-trait grouped bars of within-condition Pearson r for five reads — raw prompt projection and four post-generation poolings (mean, max, top-k, last-token) — in system and many-shot modes, 95% CIs. n = conditions per mode.

![Pooling-operator comparison bars per trait](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/3b1e7907e59c93a3b52a45c5c7cfd07cb97ab04e/figures/issue_779/r2_pooling_comparison.png)

> **Figure.** *The best pooling operator flips by trait.* Within-condition Pearson r, prompt projection vs generation-pooling reads. Mean pooling wins for sycophancy + hallucination; for evil the spike reads (last-token 0.61/0.76, max/top-k ~0.53) beat mean (0.43), and sycophancy last-token collapses (many-shot −0.05).

Interpretation:

- Reading the trait off the generation's per-token activations beats the prompt — the generation nearly contains the answer, so this is a near-ceiling reference, not a fair pre-generation monitor.
- **The best pooling operator flips by trait.** For sycophancy + hallucination (readily-expressed) mean pooling (algebraically the oracle) wins. For **evil** (sparse expression) the spike reads win: last-token **0.61/0.76** is the single best evil read, max/top-k (~0.53) also beat mean (0.43) — consistent with the plan's spike-detector hypothesis for sparse behaviors.
- Conversely, last-token is the WORST read for the readily-expressed traits (sycophancy 0.23 system, **−0.05** many-shot): the choice tracks base-expression sparsity.
- Alternative not ruled out: these reads could partly reflect nuisance structure (length, refusal style, condition identity) rather than trait content; a length/condition-control follow-up is deferred to Stage 2.

### The rig-validation gate failed, with multiple causes beyond layer selection

What is plotted (exactly): a numeric gate. Reproduced raw-projection within-condition r vs published, per trait-mode (±0.10 band); missed 4 of 6 (`gate1_all_pass = False`). The table adds raw at the oracle-selected layer vs its own best layer.

| Trait-mode | selected layer | raw @ selected | raw @ own best | published |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| evil system | L14 | 0.17 | **0.50** (L20) | 0.511 |
| evil many-shot | L14 | 0.42 | 0.62 (L19) | 0.735 |
| sycophancy system | L26 | 0.60 | 0.62 (L19) | 0.669 |
| sycophancy many-shot | L26 | 0.55 | 0.60 (L18) | 0.813 |
| hallucination system | L17 | 0.46 | **0.56** (L24) | 0.245 |
| hallucination many-shot | L17 | 0.30 | 0.53 (L27) | 0.400 |

Interpretation:

- Binding constraint: a > 0.10 miss means anchoring to Persona-Vectors' numbers is not yet trustworthy, holding the LOW tag.
- **The rig-gate failure has multiple causes.** Layer selection explains EVIL: the oracle-picked layer reads the raw projection off-layer, and evil recovers 0.17 → 0.50 at its own best layer 20 (≈ the published 0.51).
- But layer selection does NOT close the gap elsewhere. Even at PV's OWN best layer (table), sycophancy many-shot reaches only 0.60 vs the published 0.813 (0.21 short) and hallucination system 0.56, ABOVE the published 0.245 — so rig differences beyond layer choice contribute in both directions.
- Base-rate collapse is a further evil-specific factor (4 of 8 conditions prune below std 1). Reading each method at its own optimal layer AND resolving the residual rig differences are prerequisites for a MODERATE read.

# Follow-up: 3-arm TRAINING-SOURCE ablation for the context->answer-profile map h and the direct predictor g

## Goal
Test whether #779's negative R1 result (learned map h fails to beat the raw last-token projection) is caused by h's GENERIC LMSYS training corpus lacking variance along r_B, by ablating h's (and g's) TRAINING-DATA SOURCE across three arms, holding r_B and the eval rig FIXED.

## Hypothesis / mechanism
Generic LMSYS contexts rarely express the traits, so their answer profiles carry little variance along r_B; the variance-driven ridge under-fits the trait direction (evidence: #779 in-sample recon R2 ~0.83-0.86 yet the trait read trails pv_raw). Training on BEHAVIOR-VARYING contexts (both trait-high and trait-low, spanning r_B) should inject r_B-aligned variance and improve the map's trait read. Predictions: Arm B/C > Arm A on within-condition r + projection-recon; whether B/C also beat pv_raw and/or g decides whether the map has standalone value.

## Arms (SINGLE manipulated variable = h/g training-data source; r_B FIXED, extracted once, never re-extracted per arm)
- Arm A -- LMSYS only (generic; pass_b already cached). g labels via Batch-API judge pass over the 5000 (report label std; near-zero trait base rate risks a floored label).
- Arm B -- behavior-expressing only. USER DECISION (2026-07-01): use a MORE DIVERSE trait-eliciting corpus, NOT just the ~10 r_B-extraction personas (~200 low-diversity contexts, would under-power the arm and make a null ambiguous between "trait data doesn't help" and "too few/narrow contexts"). PLANNER DESIGNS THE CORPUS: many more than 10 diverse trait-eliciting persona system prompts x varied questions, sampled on-policy (temp 1.0), judge-filtered for trait expression, keeping BOTH trait-high and trait-low completions (behavior-VARYING, to span r_B). Capture per-context c_last + per-rollout v(x) at all 28 layers + judge scores. Respect the data-realism preference order; justify the synthetic-persona (tier-3) choice.
- Arm C -- LMSYS + behavior (combined; upsample behavior rows so they aren't drowned by 5000 LMSYS; report natural-mix AND 1:1).

## Both methods
- h: c_last -> v(x); read <h(c),r_B> (dot) and cosine.
- g: c_last -> trait score (matched-capacity direct predictor).

## Scaling study (added per user 2026-07-01): performance vs number of training samples, BOTH axes
Reframe the 3 arms as points on a 2D TRAINING-SIZE grid and measure learning curves along each axis, for BOTH h and g:
- N_LMSYS axis: {0, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000} (subsample the cached 5000 pass_b contexts).
- N_behavior axis: {0, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, ... up to the generated corpus max} (subsample the diverse behavior corpus; the broadening decision is what gives this axis range).
- Arm A = the N_behavior=0 slice; Arm B = the N_LMSYS=0 slice; Arm C = the interior grid cells.
- Per cell: fit h and g, report within-condition r (PRIMARY) + projection-recon + held-out recon, per trait, at the FROZEN read-out layer. Use K random subsamples per cell -> mean +/- sd error bars (a single subsample is noisy, and ridge on 3584-dim is heavily underdetermined at small N).
- Questions this answers: (1) is Arm B's result N-LIMITED or SATURATED (curve still rising vs plateaued)? -> resolves the "a null could be too-few/narrow-contexts" ambiguity directly; (2) A's N_LMSYS-dependence; (3) do behavior samples SUBSTITUTE for or COMPLEMENT LMSYS (the interaction across the 2D grid: adding behavior vs adding LMSYS at matched marginal N).
- Plots: r vs N_LMSYS (A curve), r vs N_behavior (B curve), a 2D heatmap for C, per trait x method.
- This SUBSUMES the earlier matched-N control (= the diagonal cell N_LMSYS = N_behavior) and the standalone learning-curve control.
- COMPUTE: 0-GPU (all fits on cached/generated tensors; subsampling is free). The pod GENERATION cost is UNCHANGED (generate the full diverse behavior corpus + eval rig ONCE, then subsample for every grid point).

## Eval (held out, FIXED across arms)
The persona-vectors rig eval set: 8 system + 5 ICL conditions x 20 eval questions x 10 rollouts (temp 1.0), disjoint from Arm B's training contexts on BOTH question and condition axes. Metrics: within-condition Pearson r (PRIMARY) + <h(c),r_B>-vs-oracle projection-recon + held-out reconstruction R2/cosine. Compare arms vs each other, vs pv_raw, vs g. 3 traits (evil, sycophancy, hallucination).

## Controls / confounds (carry into plan + clean-result caveats)
- Matched-N + learning curves: SUBSUMED by the 2D scaling study above (matched-N = the N_LMSYS=N_behavior diagonal; learning curves = the two axes). Use K subsamples per cell for error bars.
- Answer-multiplicity / target-noise: LMSYS trains 1 sample/context, behavior arms a 10-sample mean -- EQUALIZE (1-rollout targets both sides for the matched headline; keep the 10-rollout version too).
- Per-trait read-out layer FROZEN on a held split (selection-symmetric-nulls; do NOT read at an oracle-argmax layer selected on the eval data).
- Caveats to report: flat-vs-hierarchical training structure; ICL domain gap (behavior contexts are system-prompt-style -> expect weaker ICL than system-mode transfer); g's LMSYS label-floor.

## Consolidate the in-flight 0-GPU free-tier reads into the SAME clean-result update
- Layer-sweep (all-28-layer rerun + de-biased held-out layer selection + rig-gate recompute): eval_results/issue_779/layer_sweep.json + figures/issue_779/layer_sweep_*.png.
- Per-context reconstruction (held-out LMSYS split + projection-recon read): eval_results/issue_779/percontext_recon.json + figures/issue_779/r3_*.png.
- Held-out-question-split g (leakage-free g, held-out fold of the 20 eval questions).

## Body corrections to fold in (CONFIRMED factual errors in the current #779 body)
1. Methodology "40 eval questions per trait" -> it is 20 (the paper's 20/20 extraction/eval split; the rig monitors 20; the body's own 200-row sample = 20 x 10 proves it).
2. Methodology **Design:** claim that g is "fit on a disjoint corpus of real user prompts; the exact eval contexts are held out from h/g training" -> WRONG for the reported g (it is LOCO on the eval contexts). Correct to reflect the actual LOCO fit + the new held-out-split g.

## Compute
Arm A free. Arm B/C = a pod pass (generate the diverse behavior corpus + on-policy rollouts + judging + activation capture). Broadening the corpus takes this ABOVE the minimal ~1xH100 <=1h estimate -- planner sizes it (likely a few H100-h; under the 100-GPU-h auto-approve cap). Design references (VM /tmp, possibly transient): /tmp/issue779_3arm_design.md, /tmp/issue779_holdout_design.md.

## Rig is Persona Vectors (faithful); the ablation is #779's own
The extraction pipeline, 8 system prompts (verbatim), 5 ICL conditions, 20/20 split, last-prompt-token projection monitor, within-condition r (std<1 prune), eval prompt, and published r targets are all from arXiv 2507.21509. Standing single deviation: judge = claude-sonnet-4-5 graded 0-100 N=5 (vs the paper's GPT-4.1-mini logit-weighted scoring). The learned map h, direct predictor g, generation-side pooling, reconstruction, and THIS training-source ablation are #779 additions.

# AMENDMENT: add the pseudoinverse direction read (`pv_pinv`) to the per-arm comparison

**Routing:** fold into the CURRENT `training-source-ablation-hg` round. This is a PRE-APPROVAL plan amendment (plan v6 not yet approved as of 22:30Z). If the plan has already been approved when this is read, absorb it as an ANALYSIS-ONLY addition during implementation — it adds a read-out row, not a manipulated variable; the single-variable-change discipline (training source) is untouched. 0 GPU.

## The ask (verbatim mentor comment)
> nice, cool experiment! closely related setup -- if persona vector is v and mapping is M, could also try projecting onto `w = pseudoinverse(M) * v` (the prompt-space vector that produces the persona vector when you apply the linear map) and comparing to `w = v` baseline

## New method row `pv_pinv` (linear/ridge arm only)
- **Direction:** `w_pinv = M⁺ r_B`, where M is the fitted LINEAR (ridge) map h's weight matrix at the frozen read-out layer, per arm × trait. M⁺ = Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse via SVD. (Not applicable to the MLP h — no single weight matrix.)
- **Read:** `⟨c_last, w_pinv⟩` per eval context; PRIMARY metric = within-condition Pearson r vs the judge trait score — the identical rig/metric as the pv_raw / h / g rows. Intercepts and norms cancel in the correlation; no norm-matching needed unless a magnitude claim is made.
- **Contrast triple (report all three per arm × trait):** `w = r_B` (pv_raw — the mentor's named baseline), `w = Mᵀr_B` (the transpose ≡ the linear-h read `⟨h(c), r_B⟩`, already computed; the plan's own `r̃_B` falsification object), `w = M⁺r_B` (NEW). Why distinct: the transpose weights by σ (pullback of the read-out functional — detection); the pseudoinverse weights by 1/σ (min-norm preimage — "the prompt-space vector that produces the persona vector through the map"). They coincide only for orthogonal M, so this is a genuinely different direction, not a re-parameterization.
- **Noise-amplification guard (selection-symmetric-nulls discipline):** 1/σ amplifies ill-determined directions of a ridge-shrunk M̂. Choose the SVD truncation rank (or Tikhonov ε) on the TRAINING split only, FROZEN before the eval read; additionally report the raw full-rank pinv as a diagnostic. NO oracle selection of rank/ε on eval data.
- **Per arm:** M differs per arm (A / B / C; grid cells too if free), so `w_pinv` is per-arm — the interesting interaction is whether behavior-trained M (Arm B/C) makes the preimage direction usable where the LMSYS M (Arm A) does not.
- **Persistence:** persist the per-arm × per-trait ridge weight matrices W (+ intercepts) at the frozen layer with the round's artifacts (eval_results / HF analysis_tensors) so the pinv read is reproducible post-hoc.
- **Compute:** 0 GPU — pure linear algebra on fits the round already produces.
- **Null discipline:** the same norm-matched random-direction null the rig already runs for pv_raw applies to `pv_pinv` (a new direction read gets the same specificity bar; cf. #778's random-baseline lesson).
